reported_counterexample_reproduction.interpretation: The PBG candidate accepted this transition; P1 rejects both PARTIAL and EMPTY incidentally at missing path NONE, not through transition semantics.
P1 ignores the invalid predecessor and provides no explicit recovery classification.
The validator never mentions or discovers the contradictory manifest.

additional_observations.observation: P1 accepts proof artifacts tracked only after the claimed verified commit.
P1 accepts changed current gate or evidence bytes when no conflicting evidence checksum is present.
P1 accepts evidence text 'A0 NOT PASS' and 'A0 BYPASS' because PASS is matched as an unbounded substring.
All schema-valid matching, contradictory, and orphan VERIFIED experiment records are ignored during established-state validation.
Praxis evidence is legitimately created after its verified source commit: the gate exists at 4389885, while evidence and checksum first appear at c3e2497.

what_p1_proves: canonical project-state exists and conforms to the structural P1 schema subset
the currently resolved gate and evidence paths are files
current evidence text contains the milestone and PASS in either order on a matching line
an optional sibling checksum matches current evidence bytes when present
the declared verified commit is an ancestor of current HEAD
selected build-transience, next-authorization, and optional bootstrap checks pass
what_p1_does_not_prove: gate or evidence path is confined to the governed repository
gate or evidence existed at any declared verification-record commit
current proof bytes equal historically identified bytes
PASS text was causally produced by that execution
the transition into the current state is legitimate
experiment or milestone metadata is discovered or consistent
a repaired state explicitly preserves and explains an invalid predecessor

state_validity: Proof references resolve inside the governed repository without traversal or symlink escape.
A verification claim distinguishes verified source identity from verification-record identity.
Gate bytes are identified at an explicit source or gate commit.
Evidence bytes and structured attestation are identified at an explicit later record commit.
The record commit descends from the verified source commit and is reachable from current governed history.
A canonical state references one authoritative verification record rather than reconstructing proof from unrelated path strings.
proof_coherence: A structured attestation binds source commit, exact gate identity, invocation, exit status, result, and output digests.
PASS is a typed result derived from declared criteria, not an unbounded text search.
Historical attestation validation and current gate re-execution are distinct operations with distinct claims.
Integrity of the attestation is established through Git identity and/or recorded content digests, not an optional mutable checksum alone.
transition_validity: A new authoritative verification record explicitly references its governed predecessor or an append-only chain head.
Transition order is not inferred from lexicographic milestone names or Git ancestry alone.
Rollback cannot erase a later record; recovery or supersession must preserve the displaced history.
State validation and transition validation return separate results.
artifact_discovery_and_authority: Discovery uses explicit references or a governed registry, not an unconstrained filesystem scan.
Canonical project-state acts as the current cursor; the referenced verification record carries proof authority.
Experiment or milestone status may claim verified only through a link to the authoritative verification record, or must be treated as descriptive.
Contradiction among referenced authoritative artifacts fails closed; orphan artifacts receive no implicit authority.

recovery_semantics.observation: P1 accepts a restored valid A0 after a committed invalid partial state but records no recovery or supersession meaning.
recovery_semantics.boundary: The observation shows repair is possible, not which recovery semantics Praxis should adopt.

candidate_semantic_architecture.separation: Small composable semantic operations sharing typed records; no monolithic validator and no duplicated ontology.
